source: TESTING.md §7.7 case `curve.par.selfconsistency`, verbatim: the UST_PAR quotes { 1Y 4.00, 2Y 4.20, 3Y 4.35, 5Y 4.55, 7Y 4.70, 10Y 4.85 } (percent) at curveDate 2026-09-15, ACT/ACT, semiannual, log_linear_df. The expected values are the defining property of a bootstrap rather than an observation: every par bond that defined a node must reprice to a clean 100.000000000000 on the curve built from it, and the par rate re-implied from the curve must equal the quote to 1e-10 percent. `dfAtZero` and `nodeCount` are §7.7's additional invariants (df(0) = 1 exactly; as many nodes as inputs).

TESTING.md §7.7 case `curve.flat.analytic` — a flat 5.000 % par curve at every tenor 1Y…10Y must produce a flat 5.000 % zero curve (semiannual bond basis). The four discount factors are §7.7's closed forms 1.025^-1, 1.025^-2, 1.025^-4 and 1.025^-20, transcribed at 17 significant digits from Math.pow(1.025, -k) — NOT from this engine. NOTE: §7.7's own rendering of the fourth, `1.025⁻²⁰ = 0.610270940`, is a typo in its last two digits: 1.025^-20 is 0.6102709428588309, which rounds to 0.610270943. The closed-form expression is the pin and is asserted at §7.7's 1e-12; `df@10.printed` re-asserts the engine against §7.7's printed decimal at the 5e-9 the typo forces, so the discrepancy is recorded in the suite rather than silently dropped. `zeroPercent` and `fwdPercent` are §7.7's `zero(t) = 5.000000 %` for all t, at its 1e-10, and the same statement for every node forward.

TESTING.md §7.7 case `curve.interpolation.monotone`: the `curve.par.selfconsistency` quotes under monotone_convex and linear_zero must still reprice every input to 1e-10 — interpolation may change values between nodes, never at them — and the three interpolators must differ at t = 4 (a non-node point, the 3Y and 5Y nodes straddle it) by more than 1e-6, so a silently mis-wired interpolation cannot pass. `minimumSeparationAtT4` is §7.7's 1e-6 threshold, asserted as a floor on the pairwise |Δdf(4)|, not as an expected value. `nodeDiscountFactorsAgreeWithin` is the flip side: the three builds solve *different* node values (each shape reprices the same bond through different interior discount factors, so the 1Y node moves by ~7e-6 in df between log_linear_df and monotone_convex), but they stay inside 1e-3 of each other — a ceiling, not an observation.

WORKPLAN L503 — 'bills + par coupons → discount factors'. The three bill discount factors are the closed form of the bank-discount quote, 1 − d·days/360 (4.28 % × 28/360, 4.20 % × 91/360, 4.05 % × 182/360), transcribed at 17 significant digits; a bill's price *is* its discount factor at spot settlement, so these nodes are known rather than solved. The par quotes are the §7.7 set, and the assertion is unchanged: every par bond reprices to 100 on the curve its own quote helped build, with the bills now pinning the sub-year discount factors the 1Y and 2Y coupons interpolate through. Synthetic quotes: the bill rates are plausible 2026 levels, and the property under test holds for any arbitrage-free set.

TESTING.md §7.7 case `curve.ois.bootstrap`: SOFR OIS from seeded fixings plus par OIS rates, the same round-trip property at 1e-10, ACT/360 with daily compounding. The fixings and quotes are synthetic (§7.7 names no levels; the round trip is a property of the bootstrap, not of the quotes) and 2026-09-15 is a Tuesday, so the overnight node covers one calendar day: τ = 1/360 = 0.0027777777777777779 and df = 1/(1 + 0.0433·τ) = 0.99987973668722618, both closed forms of the published simple-interest SOFR convention. The par rates are asserted back out of the curve, and each swap's PV — annual fixed ACT/360 on T+2 modified-following SIFMA dates against a float leg that telescopes to df(start) − df(end) — is asserted at zero.
